questions.question: How many spaces are required to separate or indent statements in Robot Framework?

options.text: Two or more spaces, with four spaces recommended for clarity
Exactly two spaces, no more
options.explanation: Two spaces is the minimum, but four or more is recommended

options.text: One space is sufficient
options.explanation: Single spaces are valid characters in tokens, not separators

options.text: Tab characters must be used instead of spaces
options.explanation: While tabs work, multiple spaces are recommended to avoid editor issues

questions.question: What is a statement in Robot Framework?

options.text: A logical line containing data tokens separated by multiple spaces and ending with a line break
Any literal line in a .robot file
options.explanation: A statement can span multiple literal lines using continuation

options.text: A section header like *** Test Cases ***
options.explanation: Section headers are special; statements are within sections

options.text: Only keyword calls, not variable assignments
options.explanation: Statements include keyword calls, assignments, settings, and more

questions.question: How do you continue a statement across multiple lines in Robot Framework?

options.text: Add ... (three dots) and a separator at the beginning of the next line with same indentation
End the line with a backslash \
options.explanation: RF uses ... (three dots), not backslash for continuation

options.text: Simply continue on the next line without any marker
options.explanation: RF requires explicit continuation with ...

options.text: Use a comma at the end of the line
options.explanation: RF doesn't use commas for continuation

questions.question:
Consider these two keyword calls:

```robot
A) Keyword Call    argument one    argument two

B) Keyword Call
   ...    argument one
   ...    argument two
```

What is the relationship between these calls?

options.text: They are logically identical - the same keyword with the same arguments
Call B has three arguments while A has two
options.explanation: Both have exactly two arguments; ... is continuation, not an argument

options.text: Call B will fail due to incorrect syntax
options.explanation: This is valid continuation syntax in Robot Framework

options.text: Call A is valid but Call B passes strings '...' as arguments
options.explanation: ... is the continuation marker, not a string argument

questions.question: Which elements in Robot Framework files are written WITHOUT any indentation? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Settings in the *** Settings *** section
Test case names in the *** Test Cases *** section
Keyword names in the *** Keywords *** section
Keyword calls within test case bodies
options.explanation: Keyword calls in test bodies must be indented

options.text: Variables in the *** Variables *** section

questions.question: When defining test cases or keywords, how is the body distinguished from the name?

options.text: The name is un-indented; all body lines are indented by two or more spaces
The name is indented; body lines are un-indented
options.explanation: It's the opposite - names are un-indented, bodies are indented

options.text: Both name and body use the same indentation level
options.explanation: Different indentation levels distinguish name from body

options.text: A special marker like BEGIN and END encloses the body
options.explanation: RF uses indentation, not explicit markers

questions.question: What signals the end of a test case or keyword body?

options.text: A new un-indented test case or keyword name
A new section header like *** Keywords ***
The end of the file
A special END keyword
options.explanation: While END exists for control structures, it's not used for test/keyword bodies

options.text: An empty line
options.explanation: Empty lines don't end bodies; they're for readability

questions.question: How should content within control structures (loops, conditions) be indented for readability?

options.text: Additional four spaces beyond the control structure's indentation (recommended, not mandatory)
Same indentation as the control structure (mandatory)
options.explanation: Additional indentation is recommended but not mandatory

options.text: Control structures cannot be indented
options.explanation: Control structures and their content can and should be indented

options.text: Use curly braces instead of indentation
options.explanation: RF uses indentation, not curly braces

questions.question: Why are tabulators (\t) NOT recommended in Robot Framework files even though they are valid separators?

options.text: Different editors may align tabs to a grid making it difficult to distinguish tabs from spaces
Tabulators are completely invalid in Robot Framework
options.explanation: Tabs are valid but not recommended

options.text: Tabulators cause slower parsing performance
options.explanation: Performance is not the issue; it's about human readability

options.text: Tabulators only work in TSV format
options.explanation: Tabs work but can cause readability issues in any format

questions.question:
Analyze this code snippet:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Login Test
    Open Browser    http://example.com
    Input Text    username    admin
    Click Button    login
```

What type of token starts each body statement?

options.text: A separator token (the indentation spaces)
A keyword token
options.explanation: The keyword comes after the initial separator token

options.text: An argument token
options.explanation: Arguments come after keywords

options.text: A line break token
options.explanation: Line breaks end statements, not start them

questions.question: Are empty lines allowed in Robot Framework files?

options.text: Yes, they are allowed and encouraged for readability; they are ignored during parsing
No, empty lines cause parsing errors
options.explanation: Empty lines are allowed and ignored

options.text: Only one empty line is allowed between sections
options.explanation: Multiple empty lines are allowed anywhere

options.text: Empty lines are only allowed in *** Comments *** section
options.explanation: Empty lines are allowed throughout the file

questions.question: Where can line continuation with ... be performed? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Between a keyword name and its arguments
Between two arguments
Between a setting and its value(s)
In the middle of a keyword name
options.explanation: Continuation can only be where a separator is expected, not within a token

options.text: In the middle of a variable name
options.explanation: Continuation cannot split tokens like variable names

questions.question:
Consider this documentation example:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Documentation    This is the first line.
...    
...    This is the second line.
```

How are line breaks with continuation interpreted in documentation settings?

options.text: Single line break becomes a space; two consecutive breaks create a paragraph break
All line breaks are preserved exactly as written
options.explanation: Single breaks become spaces; use empty continuation for paragraph breaks

options.text: All line breaks are removed entirely
options.explanation: Line breaks can be preserved using empty continuation lines

options.text: Line breaks are not allowed in documentation
options.explanation: Line breaks are supported and encouraged in documentation

questions.question: How do you add an in-line comment in Robot Framework?

options.text: Add a separator (multiple spaces) followed by a hash # and the comment text
Add a single space followed by // and the comment text
options.explanation: RF uses # for comments, not //

options.text: Enclose the comment in /* */ markers
options.explanation: RF doesn't use /* */ block comments

options.text: Add a semicolon ; followed by the comment text
options.explanation: RF uses # for comments, not semicolons

questions.question:
Analyze these lines:

```robot
A) Log    Message    # This is a comment
B) # This is a full-line comment
C) Log    Hash#InMiddle    # Not a comment until here
D) Log    #StartingHash
```

Which statements are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Line A: 'This is a comment' is a comment
Line B: The entire line is a comment
Line C: 'Hash#InMiddle' contains a hash as a normal character
Line D: '#StartingHash' will be logged as-is
options.explanation: When # is preceded by a separator, it starts a comment; it needs escaping

options.text: Line C: The entire line is a comment because of the first #
options.explanation: Hash in the middle of a value is a normal character

questions.question: Does Robot Framework support block comments (multi-line comments)?

options.text: No, each line must be prefixed with # or use the *** Comments *** section
Yes, using /* to start and */ to end
options.explanation: RF doesn't support /* */ style block comments

options.text: Yes, using triple quotes """ like Python
options.explanation: RF doesn't use Python-style docstrings for comments

options.text: Yes, indent the block with extra spaces to mark it as a comment
options.explanation: Indentation doesn't create comments in RF

questions.question: What character is used to escape control characters in Robot Framework?

options.text: Backslash \
Forward slash /
options.explanation: Forward slashes are for paths, not escaping

options.text: Double quotes "
options.explanation: Quotes don't escape in RF; strings are not quoted

options.text: Caret ^
options.explanation: Caret is not used for escaping in RF

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of control characters that may need escaping in Robot Framework? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Hash # when it should be part of a value
Variable syntax ${ when it should be literal text
Multiple spaces that should be part of a value
Equal sign = used for named arguments
Period . in file names
options.explanation: Periods don't need escaping in normal usage

questions.question: If you want to use a literal backslash \ in a value, how must it be written?

options.text: As double backslash \\
As a single backslash \ (no escaping needed)
options.explanation: Backslash escapes the next character, so it must be doubled

options.text: Enclosed in quotes "\"
options.explanation: RF doesn't use quotes for escaping

options.text: As forward slash / instead
options.explanation: While recommended for paths, this changes the character

questions.question: Why is it strongly recommended to use forward slashes / instead of backslashes \ for paths in Robot Framework, even on Windows?

options.text: Because backslashes must be escaped (doubled), while forward slashes work as-is
Because backslashes don't work on Windows in Robot Framework
options.explanation: Backslashes work but require escaping

options.text: Because Robot Framework only runs on Linux
options.explanation: RF runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS

options.text: Because forward slashes are faster to parse
options.explanation: Performance is not the reason; it's about escaping complexity

questions.question: How can you include leading or trailing spaces in argument values? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Enclose the value in backslashes: \ value with spaces \
Use the ${SPACE} variable
Use double quotes: " value with spaces "
options.explanation: RF doesn't use quotes; they would become part of the value

options.text: Simply add the spaces; they are preserved automatically
options.explanation: Leading/trailing spaces are considered part of the separator

questions.question:
Analyze these Log statements:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Test Escaping
    Log    \# leading hash.
    Log    \ lead & trail \
    Log    ${SPACE}and 5 more: \ \ \ \ \
    Log    Not a \${variable}
    Log    C:\\Windows\\System32
```

What will the third Log statement output?

options.text: ' and 5 more:     ' (space at start, 5 spaces at end)
'and 5 more: \ \ \ \ \' (backslashes as-is)
options.explanation: Backslash-space becomes a literal space

options.text: 'and 5 more:' (no spaces)
options.explanation: The escaped spaces are included

options.text: Syntax error due to trailing backslashes
options.explanation: This is valid escaping syntax

questions.question: How do you pass a CSS selector starting with # (like #element_id) as an argument to a keyword?

options.text: Escape the hash: Click Element    \#element_id
No escaping needed: Click Element    #element_id
options.explanation: When # is preceded by separator, it must be escaped

options.text: Use quotes: Click Element    "#element_id"
options.explanation: Quotes become part of the value in RF

options.text: Use css= prefix: Click Element    css=#element_id
options.explanation: While this might work in SeleniumLibrary, it's a different approach, not escaping

questions.question:
Examine this test case:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Login Test
    Connect To Server
    Login User    ironman    1234567890
    Verify Valid Login    Tony Stark
    Close Server Connection
```

How many keyword calls are in this test case?

options.text: Four keyword calls
One keyword call (Login Test)
options.explanation: Login Test is the test name, not a keyword call

options.text: Three keyword calls (excluding Connect To Server)
options.explanation: Connect To Server is also a keyword call, making it four total

options.text: Seven items (test name + four keywords + two arguments)
options.explanation: The question asks for keyword calls, not all items

questions.question:
In this test case:

```robot
Login Test
    Connect To Server
    Login User    ironman    1234567890
```

How many arguments does the 'Login User' keyword receive?

options.text: Two arguments: 'ironman' and '1234567890'
One argument: 'ironman 1234567890'
options.explanation: Multiple spaces separate arguments into two distinct values

options.text: Three arguments including 'Login User'
options.explanation: 'Login User' is the keyword name, not an argument

options.text: No arguments
options.explanation: Both 'ironman' and '1234567890' are arguments

questions.question:
Analyze this code:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Password Test
    Login User    ironman    123#wrong
```

Is the hash # in '123#wrong' interpreted as a comment?

options.text: No, hashes in the middle of a value are normal characters
Yes, everything after # becomes a comment
options.explanation: Hash is only a comment marker when preceded by a separator

options.text: Yes, but it can be prevented by escaping: 123\#wrong
options.explanation: No escaping needed; hash in middle of value is literal

options.text: It causes a syntax error
options.explanation: This is valid; the hash is part of the password value

questions.question:
Consider this keyword call with continuation:

```robot
Run Keyword And Expect Error
    ...    *Invalid Password*
    ...    Login User
    ...    ironman
    ...    123
```

How many arguments does 'Run Keyword And Expect Error' receive?

options.text: Four arguments: '*Invalid Password*', 'Login User', 'ironman', '123'
One argument split across multiple lines
options.explanation: Each continued line with ... adds a separate argument

options.text: Five arguments including the ... markers
options.explanation: ... is continuation syntax, not an argument

options.text: Two arguments: the error pattern and the keyword
options.explanation: Login User's arguments (ironman, 123) are also arguments to the calling keyword

questions.question:
What is the correct indentation structure in this example?

```robot
*** Settings ***
Documentation    Suite documentation here
Resource         keywords.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Test Name
    Keyword Call    argument
    Another Keyword
```

Which statements are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Settings in *** Settings *** are not indented
Test name 'Test Name' is not indented
Keyword calls in test body are indented
Setting values like 'keywords.resource' are indented from their setting name
options.explanation: Values are separated by spaces, not indented on separate lines

questions.question:
Examine this documentation setting:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Documentation    A suite for login tests.
...    
...    Keywords are imported from the resource file.
```

What appears in the final documentation?

options.text: Two paragraphs separated by a blank line
One paragraph with all text on a single line
options.explanation: The empty continuation line creates a paragraph break

options.text: Three lines with the middle line blank
options.explanation: In documentation, the empty continuation becomes a paragraph break, not a blank line

options.text: Syntax error due to empty continuation
options.explanation: Empty continuation is valid and creates paragraph breaks

questions.question: What is the execution order of test cases in a suite file?

options.text: The order they are defined in the file, from top to bottom
Alphabetical order by test name
options.explanation: Tests execute in definition order, not alphabetical

options.text: Random order on each execution
options.explanation: Execution order is deterministic based on definition order

options.text: Priority-based using [Priority] tags
options.explanation: RF doesn't use priority-based execution by default
